observations.title: Staff Product Manager

observations.description:
Dive in and do the best work of your career at DigitalOcean. Journey alongside a strong community of top talent who are relentless in their drive to build the simplest scalable cloud. If you have a growth mindset, naturally like to think big and bold, and are energized by the fast-paced environment of a true industry disruptor, you’ll find your place here.  We value winning together—while learning, having fun, and making a profound difference for the dreamers and builders in the world. 

We’re looking for a Staff Product Security Engineer who is passionate about partnering with engineers to assess and mitigate the security risk of our virtualization stack.

You'll own the security risk posture for our virtualization stack. You'll get there by building the frameworks the org uses to reason about hypervisor risk — systematic threat models that surface risks, shared rubrics for assessing their impact and likelihood, and clear ways of communicating them to security, kernel, virtualization, and provisioning teams. From there, you'll own the response: designing and proposing defense-in-depth mitigations and driving their implementation.

As a member of the Product Security team, you will report to the Manager of Secure Design. Our Secure Design team enables DigitalOcean to build secure-by-design products. We leverage strong relationships with both product teams and the rest of security engineering to be successful. The team’s scope is primarily focused on reviewing early-stage decisions, developing threat models, scaling impact via automation, curating security patterns, authoring security guidance, training, and championing security initiatives. 

What you’ll do:

Propose and implement mitigations and defense-in-depth to threats discovered through threat modeling the virtualization stack (90%)

  • Provide deep technical expertise in systems architecture, kernel security features and network architecture to build out a threat model for our virtualization stack
  • Identify the trade-offs of different solutions and recommend the efficient design to achieve both functional goals and security requirements. We do not deliver mandates; we work alongside cross-functional partners to find mutually beneficial solutions.
  • Collaborate with development teams to implement remediations and defense in depth to protect DigitalOcean’s customers’ workloads.

Cultivate and promote a security culture (10%)

  • Mentor software engineering teams in security best practices.
  • Help oversee our vulnerability management program (we call it security debt).
  • Help DigitalOcean engineers understand how security events impact them. Do they need to worry about the next Redfish or Copy Fail CVEs? How does RetBleed impact DigitalOcean’s fleet?

What you’ll add to DigitalOcean:

Required qualifications:

  • Deep familiarity with at least one kernel security feature (ex: AppArmor, SELinux, Landlock, etc.) 
  • Capable of assessing and understanding the performance implications of code changes to virtualization stacks (especially in Qemu and KVM), built from hands-on experience. Experience 
  • A record of partnering with internal engineering teams to tackle security problems across an entire stack with empathy and creativity. Engineering teams are our partners, not our adversaries.
  • Ability to clearly communicate security topics and vulnerability classes (e.g. memory corruption, privilege escalation, TOCTOU, etc) and ability to provide actionable direction to product teams.
  • Working knowledge of modern development concepts (virtualized environments, containerization, continuous integration + delivery).

Preferred qualifications:

  • 5+ years of writing systems level code (embedded systems, kernel, assembly or similar).
  • Experience guiding software teams on secure architecture design.
  • Written code for an embedded system (raspberry pi, arduino, etc).
  • Experience building or reviewing threat models and ability to craft malicious user, attacker, and abuse/misuse cases.
  • An understanding of patches and mitigations for hardware side-channel attacks.
  • Familiarity with object oriented and functional programming concepts, particularly with languages such as Go, Rust, or C.

Compensation Range: 

  • $180,000-$215,000

*This is a remote role

DigitalOcean's Agentic AI organization provides a powerful inference cloud, Managed Agents, and robust Feedback systems that enable customers to run AI inference confidently at scale. We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to serve as a technical leader within our Feedback Systems team, driving the architecture for the massive-scale infrastructure that simulates, tests, and evaluates AI agents.
As an IC5 Staff Engineer, you will define the architectural vision for systems that simulate multi-agent, multi-turn deployments complete with tool integration. This enables customers to run and analyze "what-if" scenarios to evaluate alternative configurations for their AI agents. This is a high-impact leadership role where you will solve advanced problems at the intersection of LLM orchestration, synthetic data generation, and behavioral simulation—including defining realistic user personas from historical telemetry and structuring automated evaluation objectives and constraints. You will set the technical standard for the team and guide the engineering strategy across the Agentic AI organization.

  • Distributed Systems Expertise: Expert-level understanding of designing highly concurrent, fault-tolerant, and globally scalable backend architectures.
  • Advanced Orchestration: Deep architectural experience with stateful, durable workflow orchestration engines and managing complex asynchronous lifecycles at scale.

observations.title: Staff Software Engineer-AI

observations.description:
Dive in and do the best work of your career at DigitalOcean. Journey alongside a strong community of top talent who are relentless in their drive to build the simplest scalable cloud. If you have a growth mindset, naturally like to think big and bold, and are energized by the fast-paced environment of a true industry disruptor, you’ll find your place here.  We value winning together—while learning, having fun, and making a profound difference for the dreamers and builders in the world. 

Building AI agents that take real actions is the easy part. Building agents that get better over time — that learn from feedback, correct mistakes, and optimize toward outcomes users actually care about — is one of the hardest open problems in production AI today.

That's what this team works on. As a Staff AI/ML Engineer on our Applied Research team, you'll own the technical direction for feedback-driven learning in DigitalOcean's agentic systems: reward modeling, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, and the evaluation infrastructure needed to measure whether any of it is actually working.

This is a senior IC role with broad technical scope. You'll set direction, run experiments at scale, and close the loop between user signals and model behavior - shipping research into production, not just writing it up.

What You’ll Be Doing

Own the feedback learning roadmap

  • Define and execute the applied research agenda for feedback-driven agentic AI — from reward modeling and preference optimization to online learning and human feedback loops.
  • Translate user feedback, human evaluation data, and product signals into concrete training and optimization strategies.
  • Stay close to the research frontier on RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, GRPO, and related methods and know when to apply them versus when simpler approaches win.

Build production learning systems

  • Design and implement learning loops that improve agent reasoning, planning, tool use, and action execution over time.
  • Build evaluation frameworks that measure what matters: reasoning quality, instruction following, task success, safety, and real user outcomes — at both offline and online scale.
  • Run large-scale experiments that connect model changes to measurable improvements in user experience and business impact.

Provide technical leadership

  • Set technical direction across modeling, experimentation strategy, evaluation design, and production readiness — without requiring direct management authority.
  • Partner closely with product, engineering, design, and research teams to move work from prototype to shipped capability.
  • Communicate complex AI systems clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What You’ll Add to DigitalOcean

We're looking for engineers who have shipped real learning systems — not just prototyped them. You likely bring:

  • 8+ years of experience building production AI/ML systems — LLMs, GenAI, agentic systems, recommendation, search, personalization, or applied research at scale.
  • Hands-on experience improving AI systems through reinforcement learning, reward modeling, fine-tuning, human feedback, or preference optimization — with results you can point to.
  • Strong understanding of agentic AI: reasoning, planning, tool use, action execution, instruction following, and self-correction.
  • Strong software engineering in Python and at least one production systems language.
  • The judgment to balance model quality, product impact, latency, reliability, cost, and maintainability — and communicate those tradeoffs clearly.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong signal

  • Experience with agent evaluation, offline/online experiments, and human feedback loops in production.
  • Direct experience with RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, GRPO, or related optimization techniques.
  • Prior Staff, Senior Staff, Tech Lead, or equivalent senior IC experience.

Nice to have

  • Master's or PhD in CS, ML, AI, or a related field — or equivalent depth demonstrated through industry work.
  • Experience with production ML infrastructure: model serving, observability, data pipelines, feature stores, or experimentation platforms.
  • Research contributions via publications, patents, open-source work, or demonstrated applied research impact in RL, reward modeling, evaluation, or recommendation systems.

Compensation Range: 

  • $271,000 - $216,800

*This is a hybrid role

We are seeking a Staff Software Engineer (IC5) to join our App Platform and Functions engineering organization. App Platform is DigitalOcean’s managed PaaS: customers ship apps from source to production on Kubernetes-backed infrastructure without managing clusters themselves. Functions is our serverless compute product, running event-driven workloads on a secure, multi-tenant runtime. Together these products sit on the critical path for developers deploying and scaling modern applications—and increasingly AI and agent workloads—on DigitalOcean.

In this role, you will set technical direction for major areas of App Platform and Functions—not only within your immediate team, but across adjacent platform, networking, and compute organizations. You will define architectures that span multi-year roadmaps, drive cross-org alignment on how PaaS and serverless intersect with Kubernetes, edge, security, and AI workloads, and establish the engineering standards the team builds against. If you are a seasoned engineer who wants to combine deep technical expertise with broad organizational impact, this is the role for you.

What You’ll Do

  • Define Platform Architecture: Set technical direction for App Platform and Functions control planes and runtimes—designing for hyperscale multi-tenancy, regional distribution, and the evolving requirements of AI-native and enterprise customers. Your architecture decisions will span multiple teams and multi-year roadmaps.
  • Lead Kubernetes Product Strategy: Architect how managed Kubernetes-backed infrastructure powers customer workloads—cluster lifecycle, reconciliation, networking, isolation, autoscaling, and operational safety—balancing developer simplicity with production reliability at cloud scale.
  • Own Hard Runtime Problems: Drive solutions for high-impact platform challenges such as deployment correctness, cold-start and warm-path performance for Functions, secure workload isolation, scale-to-zero / scale-from-zero, and failure recovery across large fleets of clusters and workloads.
  • Shape Cross-Org Technical Decisions: Serve as a primary technical voice in design reviews spanning App Platform, Functions, Edge, Networking, DOKS, and adjacent product teams. Identify and resolve architectural conflicts before they become production incidents.
  • Establish Engineering Standards: Define and socialize best practices for the domain—API design, reconciliation patterns, observability, progressive delivery, and operational excellence—that raise the floor for the entire organization.
  • Mentor Senior Engineers: Coach IC2–IC4 engineers on system design, distributed systems, Kubernetes platform engineering, and technical communication; serve as a multiplier for the team’s overall capability.
  • Drive Complex Programs End-to-End: Independently lead large, ambiguous, cross-functional projects from problem framing and design through implementation, rollout, and operational ownership.
  • Translate Strategy to Leadership: Communicate platform strategy and investment rationale to senior leadership, framing technical decisions in terms of customer experience, reliability, cost efficiency, and business impact.
  • Operational Excellence: Raise the bar for production ownership—SLOs, incident response, capacity planning, and tooling—so the platform remains safe and operable as it scales.

What You’ll Add to DigitalOcean

  • Language Expert: Expert-level proficiency in Go, with deep experience building and operating gRPC/HTTP microservices at scale.
  • Kubernetes Authority: Deep knowledge of Kubernetes internals and platform patterns (controllers/operators, CRDs, scheduling, networking, multi-tenancy, cluster operations); able to design novel managed-platform systems, not just consume Kubernetes as an end user.
  • PaaS / Serverless Depth: Experience building or operating PaaS, serverless, or multi-tenant control-plane/runtime systems—ideally including deployment pipelines, lifecycle reconciliation, and production isolation models.
  • Distributed Systems Mastery: Proven ability to design and operate systems at cloud scale—handling consistency trade-offs, failure recovery, backpressure, multi-region concerns, and long-running reconciliation under real production conditions.
  • Cloud Native: Deep experience with container orchestration, SQL datastores (MySQL/Postgres), and Infrastructure as Code; experience designing systems across multiple regions and availability zones.
  • Communication & Influence: Demonstrated ability to drive technical consensus across org boundaries, mentor senior engineers, and translate platform strategy into business impact for executive audiences.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with CNI networking, service mesh, autoscaling, or scale-to-zero architectures.
  • Familiarity with function/runtime isolation technologies (containers, gVisor, Firecracker/microVMs) and cold-start optimization.
  • Experience with progressive delivery (canary / blue-green), platform SLOs, and large-scale incident management.
  • Contributions to open-source Kubernetes, CNCF, or cloud-native ecosystem projects.
  • Prior experience building developer-facing cloud products where simplicity and reliability are first-class product goals.

observations.description:

We are seeking a Staff Software Engineer (IC5) to join our Security Products team, spanning Identity and Access Management (IAM), Key Management Systems (KMS), Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM), and Identity Security Posture Management (ISPM). Security Products is the trust layer for DigitalOcean's platform — the systems you will influence protect every customer workload, every cryptographic key, every identity assertion, and every access decision made across the platform, including our rapidly growing AI inference stack.

This is not a role scoped to a single product or team. As a Staff Engineer in Security Products, you will set the technical direction across the entire security products organization, resolve architectural conflicts that no individual team can resolve alone, and build the connective tissue between identity, key management, and posture systems that makes DigitalOcean's security platform coherent rather than fragmented. You will be the primary technical partner to the Sr. Director of Security Products in shaping multi-year strategy, and you will be the engineering voice representing security architecture in DigitalOcean's most consequential platform decisions.If you are a seasoned security engineer with a track record of technical leadership that spans organizational boundaries — and who wants to define what a modern cloud security platform looks like for the AI-native era — this is the role for you.

What You'll Do

  • Define Security Products Architecture: Own the multi-year technical strategy across IAM, KMS, CSPM, and ISPM — ensuring these systems compose coherently rather than operating as isolated products. Identify the seams where identity, key management, and posture signal must integrate, and drive the architectural decisions that close them.
  • Lead the Agent Identity & Trust Architecture: Define how DigitalOcean's platform establishes, validates, and governs identity for non-human workloads — including agentic AI systems, inference pipelines, and service-to-service trust. This spans SPIFFE/SPIRE-style workload identity, short-lived credential issuance, scoped JWT attestation, and the policy engine that governs what agents are permitted to do and access.
  • Own Cross-Domain Security Platform Decisions: Serve as the primary technical arbitrator for decisions that span more than one Security Products team — including how key material is bound to identity assertions, how CSPM findings feed into access policy enforcement, how ISPM risk signals propagate into real-time authorization decisions, and how audit evidence flows across all four domains in a compliance-coherent way.
  • Shape DigitalOcean's Security Posture Strategy: Define the technical architecture for how DigitalOcean discovers, evaluates, and remediates posture risk across its platform — spanning CSPM (misconfigured infrastructure) and ISPM (over-privileged identities, orphaned credentials, policy drift). Drive the integration of posture signal into identity and access enforcement so that policy is adaptive, not static.
  • Drive Protocol and Standards Adoption: Own the technical strategy for security standards adoption across the platform — evaluating and standardizing on OIDC, SAML, SCIM, WIMSE, OAuth Token Exchange, KMIP, PKCS#11, and emerging NIST PQC standards. Represent DigitalOcean's technical interests in external standards conversations where relevant.
  • Establish Engineering Standards Across Security Products: Define and socialize cryptographic engineering practices, identity protocol patterns, policy authoring standards, and posture evaluation frameworks — raising the engineering floor across all Security Products teams and influencing the broader DO engineering organization.
  • Partner with Compliance and Executive Leadership: Translate security platform architecture into compliance posture and business impact for CISO, CPTO, and board-level audiences. Own the technical framing for HIPAA Covered Product expansion, SOC 2 control engineering, and emerging regulatory requirements as they intersect with identity and key management.
  • Mentor and Multiply: Coach IC3 and IC4 engineers across Security Products teams on system design, security engineering rigor, and cross-functional technical communication. Act as a technical multiplier — raising the capability of the organization, not just delivering individually.

What You'll Add to DigitalOcean

  • Experience: 10+ years of software engineering experience, with 5+ years of sustained focus on security-critical systems — spanning at least two of: Identity/IAM, cryptographic systems/KMS, cloud security posture, or infrastructure security — at cloud or enterprise scale.
  • Language Expert: Expert-level proficiency in Go, with deep experience building and operating security-critical, high-scale distributed services in production.
  • Identity Authority: Deep knowledge of identity protocols (OIDC, OAuth2, SAML, SCIM) and access control models (RBAC, ABAC, PBAC); able to design novel identity systems — including workload and agent identity — not just implement existing patterns.
  • Cryptography Authority: Sound applied cryptography fundamentals — symmetric and asymmetric primitives, key derivation hierarchies, authenticated encryption, envelope encryption patterns — and a track record of designing cryptographic systems correctly under real operational constraints.
  • Posture Systems: Experience designing or operating CSPM or ISPM systems — including resource discovery, policy evaluation at scale, misconfiguration detection, and risk signal aggregation. Familiarity with cloud resource models (DigitalOcean, AWS, GCP, or Azure) and the control frameworks that govern them (CIS Benchmarks, NIST CSF, or equivalent).
  • Cross-Domain Integration: Demonstrated ability to design systems where identity, key management, and posture signals compose — rather than operating in isolation. Candidates who have worked at the intersection of two or more of these domains are strongly preferred.
  • Distributed Systems Mastery: Proven ability to design and operate systems at cloud scale — handling consensus, replication, partitioning, and failure recovery under real production conditions — with security and auditability as first-class constraints.
  • Organizational Influence: Track record of driving technical alignment across multiple engineering teams or organizations — including resolving architectural conflicts, establishing cross-team standards, and influencing roadmaps beyond your direct area of ownership.
  • Communication: Demonstrated ability to translate complex security platform strategy into business impact and compliance posture for executive and board-level audiences.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Open Policy Agent (OPA), Rego, or other policy-as-code frameworks at production scale.
  • Familiarity with SPIFFE/SPIRE, WIMSE, or other workload identity frameworks.
  • Experience with HSMs (Thales/Luna, AWS CloudHSM, or equivalent) and production-grade key management platforms.
  • Familiarity with post-quantum cryptography standards (NIST PQC: ML-KEM, ML-DSA) and migration planning for production key hierarchies.
  • Experience with PKCS#11, KMIP, or other KMS/HSM interoperability standards.
  • Background contributing to open-source security projects or engaging with standards bodies (IETF, OpenID Foundation, NIST).
  • Prior experience designing security platform strategy for AI-native or inference-heavy workloads.
  • Background supporting HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or FedRAMP compliance programs from an engineering ownership perspective.

*This job is located in Bengaluru, India

As a Staff Technical Product Marketing Manager, you will own the technical go-to-market for your area end to end, driven from two angles: the products (one or more of our AI-Native Cloud product lines) and the markets they serve (use cases, verticals, segments). You set the standard for how technical product marketing is executed on this team, on our stages, and in our most important executive moments. You are the person who decides not just what we built, but who it is for, what it replaces, and why it matters to them.

What you'll do

  • Own the narrative and be our market authority. Set positioning and messaging across your area (product and market), grounded in provable value, not benchmark theater or per-token cost wars. Serve as the go-to positioning authority for Product Marketing, Sales, DevRel, and executive leadership, backed by a real-time view of frontier labs, hyperscalers, inference providers, and neoclouds.
  • Build the proof yourself. Create technical demos, sample apps, and code (Python, JavaScript) that show the platform working. You don't wait for an engineer to explain a feature; you test it.

Define success metrics before launch, not after. Give AEs and Solutions Engineers the talk tracks, demo environments, and battlecards to close high-value AI deals. Build a repeatable launch playbook, and measure impact through adoption, pipeline, deal velocity, and win rates.

  • Public voice. Proven ability to represent complex technical products on stage and in high-visibility content, with credibility in front of engineers, customers, analysts, and executives.

  • Drive value delivery across your assigned programs and special projects, including prioritization, planning, risk management, execution, and measurement of success. You'll own delivery of your programs and deliverables with guidance from your manager and senior TPMs, and lead defined workstreams on larger, more complex programs
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and infrastructure leads throughout the life of the program on value delivery and process/practice improvements
  • Keep supply chain, facilities, hardware engineering, colocation providers, remote hands, and internal networking teams informed and aligned on the schedules for your programs, coordinating the steps from site and capacity planning through deployment
  • Build relationships within and across teams to lead stakeholders toward a common goal; facilitate team and cross-functional meetings that foster decision-making across multiple teams and locations, and help your team prioritize work
  • Communicate clearly and often about program requirements, timelines, objectives, status, risks, technical concepts, and process, so that expectations are understood and supported by both internal and external stakeholders
  • Own the follow-through on your programs: tracking commitments across teams and vendors, checking in before a date slips, and closing the loop on open questions and decisions so nothing falls through the cracks
  • Help your team identify, capture, and manage risks, recognizing risk early, whether a delayed hardware shipment or a facility constraint, and forming mitigation plans as required
  • Proactively manage changes in scope and priority shifts, and aid in resolving impediments, conflicts, and competing priorities for your team and across teams, working unplanned issues to resolution with support as appropriate
  • Suggest improvements to team processes and help implement the repeatable ways of working (and the visibility behind them) that get infrastructure online faster and improve reliability

What You'll Add to DigitalOcean:

Core to the role:

  • Experience keeping cross-functional work on track in a fast-paced environment: planning it, spotting what's about to slip, resolving what blocks it, and driving it to done. You don't need to have held the "Technical Program Manager" title; we're interested in people who've done this work under other names, including project or delivery management, data center or deployment operations, facilities or construction project management, supply chain or capacity planning, and technical business operations
  • Personable yet persistent, with authentic interpersonal interactions. You're comfortable being the person who follows up, and follows up again, without wearing out your welcome
  • An understanding of what qualifies as a risk, and how to capture and manage risks appropriately for your team
  • Ability to identify and clearly state problems that arise within your team, think critically about the stated need versus the underlying cause, gather necessary data, and to suggest and help implement solutions
  • Ability to distill complex or technical concepts into clear, structured communications and action plans, balancing a detail- and process-oriented mindset with a focus on outcomes
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and facilitation skills: building productive relationships and managing expectations, looking for areas of agreement, and hearing the concerns that go unvoiced
  • Ability to influence and work through others where direct reporting relationships do not exist, acting as a bridge between deeply technical teams and operational teams
  • Comfortable using AI tools to take the toil out of your daily work, whether drafting and tightening status communications, summarizing long threads and meetings, or synthesizing scattered information into a clear picture

Also valuable:

  • Experience in physical infrastructure, hardware, facilities, or data center environments
  • Familiarity with the infrastructure context: data center and hardware fundamentals such as rack space, power, cooling, and deployment workflows; the procurement lifecycle and its long lead times; and the basics of the AI/ML hardware space, including why customers use GPUs and the high-level difference between training and inference. Depth in all of these isn't expected
  • Experience with project management tooling (e.g., the Atlassian suite/Jira and Confluence), including creating and updating items, dashboards and basic querying, and building roadmaps

Compensation Range:

You’ll be a part of a cutting-edge technology company with an upward trajectory, who are proud to simplify cloud and AI so builders can spend more time creating software that changes the world. As a member of the team, you will be a Shark who thinks big, bold, and scrappy, like an owner with a bias for action and a powerful sense of responsibility for customers, products, employees, and decisions.

Pantheon’s WebOps Platform powers more than 300,000 websites for organizations including Google, Princeton, Salesloft, and Doctors Without Borders. Our platform helps developers and marketers build, manage, and scale WordPress and Drupal websites faster.

The Role

Our BDRs create the first meaningful connection between Pantheon and future customers. You’ll research priority accounts, find the right people, understand their business challenges,
and create qualified pipeline for our Account Executive team. 

This is not a generic, high-volume outreach role. It’s a research-led, account-based role for someone who can turn insight into relevant conversations. You’ll use phone, email, social selling, referrals, and events to reach decision-makers and build relationships across strategic accounts.

What You Need to Succeed 

  • Own a portfolio of target accounts and prioritize where to focus.
  • Research companies, technologies, organizational changes, business priorities, and buying signals.
  • Map stakeholders and multi-thread conversations across strategic accounts.
  • Write and deliver concise, personalized outreach across multiple channels.
  • Cold call prospects and lead initial qualification and discovery conversations.
  • Understand priorities, pain points, urgency, stakeholders, and fit.
  • Partner with Account Executives on account plans, qualification, handoffs, and next steps.
  • Collaborate with Marketing on campaigns, messaging, content, and account insights.
  • Keep Salesforce and account intelligence accurate and actionable.
  • Test, learn, and improve your approach based on conversion and pipeline data. 

How AI Fits into the Work

AI is part of our modern BDR workflow. You’ll use approved tools to:

  • Summarize account research and surface relevant signals.
  • Prioritize accounts and contacts.
  • Create first-pass account briefs, messaging angles, and call preparation.
  • Analyze engagement, conversion, and pipeline progression.
  • Improve team playbooks and repeatable workflows.

AI supports your judgment—it does not replace it. You’ll verify facts, edit every message, protect confidential information, follow Pantheon policies, and never send unreviewed AI-generated outreach.

How We Measure Success

Activity matters, but quality matters more. We look at:

  • Qualified pipeline sourced and accepted by Sales.
  • Conversion from outreach to meaningful conversations and opportunities.
  • Account engagement and multi-threading.
  • Opportunity quality and progression after handoff.
  • Research quality, messaging relevance, CRM hygiene, and follow-through.
  • Consistent achievement of agreed goals.

What You Bring to the Table

  • 12+ months of experience in sales development, business development, outbound prospecting, or a related sales role.
  • A track record of holding your role, managing goals, and improving performance.
  • Strong account research, writing, phone, and social-selling skills.
  • Curiosity about technology and how digital teams work.
  • An analytical, coachable, resourceful approach.
  • Strong organization across multiple accounts and stakeholders.
  • Comfort using AI and sales technology thoughtfully and responsibly.
  • A collaborative mindset and genuine interest in building a long-term GTM career.

  • SaaS, WebOps, digital experience, MarTech, cloud, or enterprise sales experience.
  • Experience with Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, Gong, Nooks, or similar tools.
  • Experience with ABM, strategic prospecting, multi-threading, or enterprise sales.
  • Experience using AI to improve research, writing, analysis, or workflow design.

Growth at Pantheon 

We build durable skills, not just activity metrics. You’ll receive coaching, training, sales technology, and feedback on your research, messaging, conversations, and pipeline outcomes. Strong performance can create opportunities in Senior BDR, Account Executive, Account-Based Marketing, Revenue Operations, and other GTM roles. Progression is based on demonstrated capability, sustained performance, and business needs.

We have all the usual perks and benefits but what we can really offer you is a fantastic work environment powered by an amazing team.

observations.description:
About Pantheon

Pantheon brings together exceptional builders who take ownership, drive meaningful impact, and shape what's next for the web. We power more than 300,000 websites globally for organizations including Google, Princeton, Salesloft, Clorox, and the United Nations. Every day, thousands of developers and marketers use our WebOps platform to build, iterate, and scale WordPress, Drupal, and Next.js sites that reach billions of people worldwide. As an employer, we operate with the same philosophy that drives our product: foundation and freedom. Pantheon is a vibrant, remote-forward team of experts who care deeply about their craft and results. Here, you take ownership of work that matters, contribute alongside exceptional people, and see the impact you create.

The Role

We are looking for a Principal Engineer to provide technical leadership and help define engineering strategy and best practices across Pantheon.

Our Collaborative Web Platform is a zero-to-one product at the intersection of real-time collaboration, visual editing, web application infrastructure, developer experience, AI-assisted workflows, content management, and governed publishing. The product must make it possible for multiple roles—and increasingly, AI agents—to work in parallel without compromising reliability, security, accessibility, brand standards, or the live site.

This is a high-leverage individual contributor role. You will remain hands-on while operating across product and organizational boundaries: shaping architecture, resolving the hardest technical decisions, establishing engineering standards, and helping teams build a production-ready platform that can evolve safely.

What You Will Do

Define technical direction

  • Own and evolve the architectural vision across real-time collaboration, branch-aware content state, APIs, data models, visual editing, publishing, integrations, and developer-facing extension points.
  • Establish clear architectural boundaries between our collaborative web platform, Pantheon’s hosting and platform capabilities, and external systems.
  • Make pragmatic build-versus-buy and platform-boundary decisions using explicit criteria for customer value, reliability, security, operational complexity, developer experience, and total cost of ownership.
  • Identify architectural risks early, make tradeoffs explicit, and ensure decisions are documented, communicated, and revisited when evidence changes.
  • Create an architecture that supports fast MVP delivery without locking the company into avoidable long-term constraints.

Drive company-wide engineering strategy

  • Partner with engineering, product, design, security, infrastructure, support, and go-to-market leaders to define technical strategy for capabilities that span multiple organizations.
  • Translate company and product goals into a coherent engineering strategy, including sequencing, investment areas, platform responsibilities, and measurable outcomes.
  • Help establish common engineering principles for reliability, security, privacy, observability, API design, testing, deployment, incident response, and operational ownership.
  • Define when engineering standards should be centralized, when teams should have autonomy, and how exceptions are evaluated and recorded.
  • Create lightweight mechanisms for cross-team technical alignment, such as architecture reviews, decision records, reference patterns, technical roadmaps, and dependency planning.
  • Represent engineering in company-level discussions where technical choices affect customer experience, product strategy, operating cost, or delivery risk.

Raise the engineering quality bar

  • Establish practical best practices for designing, building, testing, deploying, and operating production software.
  • Promote reliability-by-design: service ownership, clear SLOs, actionable telemetry, safe migrations, failure-mode analysis, graceful degradation, retry safety, idempotency, and tested rollback paths.
  • Improve the consistency and quality of design documents, technical proposals, API contracts, code reviews, test strategies, and release plans.
  • Help teams distinguish reversible decisions from durable commitments and match review depth to the risk of the decision.
  • Set expectations for secure defaults, least-privilege access, dependency management, threat modeling, and responsible use of AI in engineering workflows and product capabilities.
  • Use operational data, customer impact, incident learning, and delivery signals to guide improvements rather than relying on opinion or process for its own sake.

Build technical leverage across teams

  • Mentor Staff and Senior engineers through architecture reviews, design sessions, pairing, code reviews, and direct feedback.
  • Help engineers grow their ability to reason about system boundaries, tradeoffs, operational risk, and customer impact.
  • Build reusable patterns, libraries, templates, documentation, and paved paths that make the right engineering behavior easier.
  • Reduce duplicated discovery and inconsistent implementation across teams by making important technical context easy to find and apply.
  • Contribute hands-on code where it is the best way to validate an architectural direction, unblock a critical path, or establish a reference implementation.
  • Strengthen the technical hiring bar and help design interview signals for senior and principal-level engineering impact.

Partner with product and customers

  • Work closely with product and design to turn ambiguous product problems into technically coherent, phased delivery plans.
  • Push back on scope, sequencing, or technical assumptions when the data indicates customer, reliability, or execution risk.
  • Participate in selected customer, partner, and internal technical discussions to understand real-world constraints and validate architectural choices.
  • Ensure that developer experience, content-team experience, and operational experience are treated as first-class product concerns.

What You Bring

  • 14+ years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent depth demonstrated through sustained technical impact.
  • A track record of acting as a Principal Engineer, Chief Architect or equivalent technical leader across multiple teams and products.
  • Experience defining technical strategy for a complex product, platform, or distributed system from early architecture through production operation.
  • Strong systems thinking and the ability to reason across frontend, backend, APIs, data, infrastructure, security, and operations.
  • Experience with distributed, event-driven, real-time, collaborative, or stateful systems.
  • Demonstrated judgment in build-versus-buy decisions, platform boundaries, technical investment, and managing technical debt.
  • Deep experience with production reliability, observability, incident response, safe delivery, and operational ownership.
  • Strong API and integration design experience, including versioning, compatibility, authentication, authorization, webhooks, or extension models.
  • The ability to write clear design documents and explain complex tradeoffs to engineers, executives, product partners, customers, and non-technical stakeholders.
  • A history of mentoring senior engineers and influencing technical direction without relying on formal authority.
  • Comfort working in ambiguity, moving between strategy and implementation, and changing direction when evidence warrants it.
  • Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools thoughtfully, with attention to quality, security, auditability, and failure handling.

Helpful Experience

  • Real-time collaboration, multiplayer systems, CRDTs, operational transformation, synchronization, or conflict resolution.
  • Visual editors, page builders, content platforms, CMS products, web publishing, developer tooling, SDKs, or plugin ecosystems.
  • Cloud-native systems built on platforms such as GCP, AWS, or Cloudflare.
  • Modern web application architecture using technologies such as TypeScript, Node.js, React, Next.js, or comparable ecosystems.
  • Multi-tenant SaaS products with strong requirements for governance, security, availability, and customer isolation.
  • Leading technical strategy across teams during a zero-to-one product launch or a significant platform transformation.

Why This Role Matters

Our collaborative web platform's most consequential technical decisions cross normal team boundaries. The Principal Engineer will provide the connective tissue between product ambition and engineering execution: ensuring that we can move quickly while maintaining architectural coherence, operational safety, and a foundation that the rest of Pantheon can build on.

This role is ideal for an engineer who wants broad technical impact without leaving the work behind—someone who can set direction across the company, earn trust through sound judgment, and still open the editor, inspect the trace, review the pull request, or write the critical piece of code.

What We Offer

We have all the usual perks and benefits but what we can really offer you is a fantastic work environment powered by an amazing team.

  • Industry competitive compensation and equity plan
  • Flexible time off, sick days, and 13 paid holidays
  • Comprehensive medical insurance including Health, Dental and Vision
  • Paid parental leave (plus fertility, adoption and other family planning benefits)
  • In-office workspace (San Francisco & Chicago)
  • Monthly allowance for wellness, reading and access to LinkedIn Learning for continued development
  • Events and activities both team-based and company wide that inspire, educate and cultivate

Pantheon is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome applications from all backgrounds regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, disability, or any other classification protected by law. Pantheon complies with federal and local disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation due to a disability for any part of the interview process, please contact talent@pantheon.io. Pursuant to local and federal regulations, Pantheon will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment.

After an offer is made and accepted, E-verify will be utilized to establish your identity and employment eligibility as required by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

  • Establish clear architectural boundaries between our collaborative web platform, Pantheon’s hosting and platform capabilities, and external systems.
  • Make pragmatic build-versus-buy and platform-boundary decisions using explicit criteria for customer value, reliability, security, operational complexity, developer experience, and total cost of ownership.
  • Identify architectural risks early, make tradeoffs explicit, and ensure decisions are documented, communicated, and revisited when evidence changes.
  • Create an architecture that supports fast MVP delivery without locking the company into avoidable long-term constraints.

Drive company-wide engineering strategy

  • Partner with engineering, product, design, security, infrastructure, support, and go-to-market leaders to define technical strategy for capabilities that span multiple organizations.
  • Translate company and product goals into a coherent engineering strategy, including sequencing, investment areas, platform responsibilities, and measurable outcomes.
  • Help establish common engineering principles for reliability, security, privacy, observability, API design, testing, deployment, incident response, and operational ownership.
  • Define when engineering standards should be centralized, when teams should have autonomy, and how exceptions are evaluated and recorded.
  • Create lightweight mechanisms for cross-team technical alignment, such as architecture reviews, decision records, reference patterns, technical roadmaps, and dependency planning.
  • Represent engineering in company-level discussions where technical choices affect customer experience, product strategy, operating cost, or delivery risk.

Raise the engineering quality bar

  • Establish practical best practices for designing, building, testing, deploying, and operating production software.
  • Promote reliability-by-design: service ownership, clear SLOs, actionable telemetry, safe migrations, failure-mode analysis, graceful degradation, retry safety, idempotency, and tested rollback paths.
  • Improve the consistency and quality of design documents, technical proposals, API contracts, code reviews, test strategies, and release plans.
  • Help teams distinguish reversible decisions from durable commitments and match review depth to the risk of the decision.
  • Set expectations for secure defaults, least-privilege access, dependency management, threat modeling, and responsible use of AI in engineering workflows and product capabilities.
  • Use operational data, customer impact, incident learning, and delivery signals to guide improvements rather than relying on opinion or process for its own sake.

Build technical leverage across teams

  • Mentor Staff and Senior engineers through architecture reviews, design sessions, pairing, code reviews, and direct feedback.
  • Help engineers grow their ability to reason about system boundaries, tradeoffs, operational risk, and customer impact.
  • Build reusable patterns, libraries, templates, documentation, and paved paths that make the right engineering behavior easier.
  • Reduce duplicated discovery and inconsistent implementation across teams by making important technical context easy to find and apply.
  • Contribute hands-on code where it is the best way to validate an architectural direction, unblock a critical path, or establish a reference implementation.
  • Strengthen the technical hiring bar and help design interview signals for senior and principal-level engineering impact.

Partner with product and customers

  • Work closely with product and design to turn ambiguous product problems into technically coherent, phased delivery plans.
  • Push back on scope, sequencing, or technical assumptions when the data indicates customer, reliability, or execution risk.
  • Participate in selected customer, partner, and internal technical discussions to understand real-world constraints and validate architectural choices.
  • Ensure that developer experience, content-team experience, and operational experience are treated as first-class product concerns.

What You Bring

  • 14+ years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent depth demonstrated through sustained technical impact.
  • A track record of acting as a Principal Engineer, Chief Architect or equivalent technical leader across multiple teams and products.
  • Experience defining technical strategy for a complex product, platform, or distributed system from early architecture through production operation.
  • Strong systems thinking and the ability to reason across frontend, backend, APIs, data, infrastructure, security, and operations.
  • Experience with distributed, event-driven, real-time, collaborative, or stateful systems.
  • Demonstrated judgment in build-versus-buy decisions, platform boundaries, technical investment, and managing technical debt.
  • Deep experience with production reliability, observability, incident response, safe delivery, and operational ownership.
  • Strong API and integration design experience, including versioning, compatibility, authentication, authorization, webhooks, or extension models.
  • The ability to write clear design documents and explain complex tradeoffs to engineers, executives, product partners, customers, and non-technical stakeholders.
  • A history of mentoring senior engineers and influencing technical direction without relying on formal authority.
  • Comfort working in ambiguity, moving between strategy and implementation, and changing direction when evidence warrants it.
  • Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools thoughtfully, with attention to quality, security, auditability, and failure handling.

Helpful Experience

  • Real-time collaboration, multiplayer systems, CRDTs, operational transformation, synchronization, or conflict resolution.
  • Visual editors, page builders, content platforms, CMS products, web publishing, developer tooling, SDKs, or plugin ecosystems.
  • Cloud-native systems built on platforms such as GCP, AWS, or Cloudflare.
  • Modern web application architecture using technologies such as TypeScript, Node.js, React, Next.js, or comparable ecosystems.
  • Multi-tenant SaaS products with strong requirements for governance, security, availability, and customer isolation.
  • Leading technical strategy across teams during a zero-to-one product launch or a significant platform transformation.

Why This Role Matters

Our collaborative web platform's most consequential technical decisions cross normal team boundaries. The Principal Engineer will provide the connective tissue between product ambition and engineering execution: ensuring that we can move quickly while maintaining architectural coherence, operational safety, and a foundation that the rest of Pantheon can build on.

This role is ideal for an engineer who wants broad technical impact without leaving the work behind—someone who can set direction across the company, earn trust through sound judgment, and still open the editor, inspect the trace, review the pull request, or write the critical piece of code.

What We Offer

We have all the usual perks and benefits but what we can really offer you is a fantastic work environment powered by an amazing team.

  • Events and activities both team-based and company wide that inspire, educate and cultivate

observations.description:
About Pantheon

Pantheon WebOps Platform powers the open web, running more than 300,000 sites in the cloud for customers including Google, Princeton, Salesloft, and Doctors Without Borders.

Every day, thousands of developers and marketers create, iterate, and scale WordPress and Drupal sites to reach billions of people globally.

Pantheon’s multitenant, container-based platform enables organizations to manage all of their websites from a single dashboard. Organizations including Clorox and the United Nations drive results through accelerated development and real-time publishing using Pantheon’s collaborative workflows.

The Role

As a Sales Engineer at Pantheon, you will partner closely with Sales Account Teams to demonstrate the value and technical capabilities of the Pantheon platform.

This role is designed for a hands-on practitioner who can build, troubleshoot, explain, and sell modern web experiences. You will translate complex technical requirements into clear, compelling solutions and help prospects understand how Pantheon can support their business goals.

You will be part of a founding team bringing a promising new product to market—one with the potential to disrupt an established category. Because the team is building the product, market, and sales motion at the same time, you may occasionally need to work outside the traditional boundaries of the Sales Engineer role—helping create demos, improve documentation, shape messaging, support early customers, or solve whatever problem is most important that week.

You will play a critical role in qualifying and closing customers while working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Customer teams, and agency partners. You will help onboard design and development teams at client and partner organizations, enabling them to understand the product, build effectively, and deliver successful customer experiences. You will influence how prospects, clients, and partners understand and adopt Pantheon, contribute field insight to product direction, and help evolve how Pantheon positions its technical value in the market.

The Sales Engineer owns technical discovery, solution design, demonstrations, and the technical win. Implementation Engineers may support deeper configuration, development, and delivery work, but the Sales Engineer must be technically credible enough to build and debug demonstrations, understand architectural tradeoffs, and earn the trust of technical buyers.

What you’ll do

  • Partner effectively with Account Executives to uncover customer needs and map solutions to business outcomes in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

  • Identify, surface, and resolve technical blockers throughout the sales cycle.
  • Complete RFPs, RFIs, and security and technical questionnaires in support of procurement processes.
  • Clearly articulate return on investment and technical value to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Customer teams to influence platform direction and customer experience.
  • Secure the technical win for assigned opportunities.
  • Develop and maintain subject matter expertise in key technical areas, particularly modern web infrastructure, composable architectures, and AI-assisted development.
  • Contribute to internal enablement by sharing customer insights, field learnings, demonstrations, and best practices across teams.

What you bring to the table

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience developing, deploying, or supporting modern websites and web applications, including customer-facing technical work.
  • Experience developing on Drupal, WordPress, and React/Next.js.
  • Comfort with AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, including using them to build, debug, and iterate on working web experiences.
  • Strong presentation and facilitation skills, including the ability to lead compelling technical demonstrations and explain architectural tradeoffs clearly.
  • Ability to translate technical concepts into clear business value.
  • Strong technical curiosity and a continuous learning mindset.
  • Comfort working with evolving products, incomplete documentation, and early customer feedback.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to have

  • Experience with decoupled content stores such as Contentful or Sanity.
  • Experience with headless or decoupled architectures.
  • Deep experience with Next.js or other modern JavaScript web frameworks.
  • Contributions to open-source projects, especially in the WordPress, Drupal, React, or Next.js ecosystems.

What We Offer 

We have all the usual perks and benefits but what we can really offer you is a fantastic work environment powered by an amazing team.

  • Industry competitive compensation and equity plan
  • Flexible time off, sick days, and 13 paid holidays
  • Comprehensive medical insurance including Health, Dental and Vision
  • Paid parental leave (plus fertility, adoption and other family planning benefits)
  • In-office workspace (San Francisco & Chicago)
  • Monthly allowance for wellness, reading and access to LinkedIn Learning for continued development
  • Events and activities both team-based and company wide that inspire, educate and cultivate

Compensation

The OTE range for this position is USD $123,000 – $153,900.

Final compensation will be determined based on factors including role scope, relevant experience, and geographic location.

 

Pantheon is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome applications from all backgrounds regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, disability, or any other classification protected by law. Pantheon complies with federal and local disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities. Pursuant to local and federal regulations, Pantheon will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment.

After an offer is made and accepted, E-verify will be utilized to establish your identity and employment eligibility as required by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

About Pantheon

Pantheon brings together exceptional builders who take ownership, drive meaningful impact, and shape what's next for the web. We power more than 300,000 websites globally for organizations including Google, Princeton, Salesloft, Clorox, and the United Nations. Here, you take ownership of work that matters, contribute alongside exceptional people, and see the impact you create.

The Role 

As the Senior Engineering Manager for Customer Runtimes, you will lead and manage a sizable team of talented software engineers focused on building the scaled infrastructure services that run the high-impact Drupal, Wordpress, and Next.js sites of our customers. The team is driving an exciting transformation of our most core customer infrastructure to expand our capabilities, leverage best of breed open source technologies, and significantly reduce toil. This critical role is responsible for the health and progress of our largest infrastructure footprint.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and Mentor: Guide the team through organizational changes, challenges, and uncertainties, maintaining productivity and morale. Drive the team's success with hands-on coaching, guidance, and troubleshooting, as you are passionate about mentoring and developing engineering talent.
  • Execution and Delivery: Manage multiple critical projects with shifting priorities and ensure the team adapts quickly to evolving processes to deliver high-quality work, while considering potential oncall and operational burden.
  • Strategy and Vision: Understand the organization’s objectives and direction, aligning the team’s priorities accordingly. You will advocate for changes that benefit the team and the broader organization.
  • Technical Guidance: Lead architecture discussions, review critical code, provide constructive feedback, and contribute to technical discussions to maintain a high bar for technical excellence.
  • Collaboration: Craft team and organizational goals, working with immediate team members and cross-functional stakeholders (10-20 individuals) to ensure alignment.
  • Communication: Clear, confident communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts effectively both verbally and written.
  • Direction: Provide clear direction to your team, translating high-level goals into actionable tasks, providing feedback, and ensuring everyone is aligned. You will have autonomy within your team's scope to decide how to allocate work and solve problems while aligning with the overall engineering strategy.

What You’ll Bring to the Table

Experience

  • 12+ years of experience in software development, with a solid foundation as a Staff or Principal engineer demonstrating deep technical expertise.
  • 3+ years of direct people management experience, including large global teams, mentoring Staff engineers, and balancing multiple subteams.
  • Track record of driving performance management and cultivating a high-performance engineering culture, setting clear expectations, delivering candid feedback, and developing engineers at all levels through structured growth and calibration processes.
  • Proven ability to deliver multiple simultaneous projects successfully, working directly with customers and external communities.
  • Leading cloud and infrastructure modernization initiatives that span large critical fleets.
  • AI-native instincts: fluency with AI coding assistants and a point of view on how they change how teams work.
  • Strong practitioner of Agile, Scrum, or other structured development methodologies.

Technical Acumen

  • Direct experience designing platforms running cloud-based applications at broad scale.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems, scalable cloud architectures and cloud technologies, including orchestration services (e.g. Kubernetes/K8S, GCP GKE, AWS ECS/EKS), application services (e.g. Google Cloud Run, AWS Lambda), relational databases (e.g. MySQL, MariaDB, Cloud SQL), and application caches (e.g. Redis, Memcached).
  • Production experience running and automating large Linux-based fleets using both Infrastructure-as-Code tools like Terraform and dynamic provisioning systems.
  • Deep understanding of computer science fundamentals, including data structures and algorithms.
  • Working knowledge of Python, Golang, or other modern programming languages.

What We Offer

We have all the usual perks and benefits but what we can really offer you is a fantastic work environment powered by an amazing team.

  • Industry competitive compensation and equity plan
  • Paid Time Off (PTO), Paid Sick Leave (PSL) and 12 Paid Company Holidays
  • Full medical coverage (Extended health care, dental, vision)
  • Top-of-line equipment
  • In-office workspace (Vancouver, BC Canada)
  • Monthly allowance for wellness, reading and access to LinkedIn Learning for continued development
  • Events and activities both team-based and company wide that inspire, educate and cultivate

Pantheon is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome applications from all backgrounds regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, disability, or any other classification protected by law. observations.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Customer Runtimes

observations.description:
About Pantheon

Pantheon WebOps Platform powers the open web, running more than 300,000 sites in the cloud for customers including Google, Princeton, Salesloft, and Doctors Without Borders. Every day, thousands of developers and marketers create, iterate, and scale WordPress and Drupal sites to reach billions of people globally. Pantheon’s multitenant, container-based platform enables organizations to manage all of their websites from a single dashboard. Organizations, including Clorox and the United Nations, drive results through accelerated development and real-time publishing using Pantheon’s collaborative workflows.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior GTM Growth Marketer to join a team that operates with the pace and mindset of a startup within Pantheon. You'll help identify, develop, and scale growth opportunities while bringing innovative, differentiated solutions to market.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in ambiguity, thinks in hypotheses, and enjoys turning market signals into actionable GTM strategies. As a member of this small, startup-style growth team, you'll partner closely with Product Marketing, Sales, and Product to better understand customers, test new approaches, and build repeatable GTM strategies that accelerate growth.

This is not a traditional demand generation role. We're looking for a builder who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution. Someone who can analyze customer feedback, sales conversations, and market signals to continuously improve our GTM approach.

What You Need to Succeed 

GTM Strategy & Experimentation

  • Develop and execute experiments to identify ideal customer profiles, target segments, messaging, and growth opportunities
  • Define experiment goals, success metrics, and learning frameworks to understand what is working and why
  • Build an evolving understanding of target customers, market segments, objections, and buying signals
  • Translate insights into actionable recommendations for Sales, Product Marketing, and Product teams

Growth Programs & Market Development

  • Build and iterate growth programs across channels including outbound, digital campaigns, LinkedIn, account-based approaches, and other emerging tactics
  • Identify opportunities to increase awareness and engagement within target markets
  • Create repeatable processes for testing, learning, and scaling GTM motions
  • Own measurement frameworks that surface insights and business impact, not just activity metrics

Customer & Sales Insights

  • Partner closely with Sales teams to understand customer conversations, objections, buying patterns, and market feedback
  • Analyze customer and sales insights to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement
  • Translate field insights into messaging improvements, campaign strategies, and GTM recommendations
  • Serve as the connection point between what the market is saying and how we position our solutions

Sales & Marketing Enablement

  • Develop and refine messaging, outreach approaches, talk tracks, and supporting materials based on market learnings
  • Partner with Product Marketing to improve positioning and communicate value effectively
  • Work closely with Sales partners to understand what resonates and continuously improve our approach

GTM Operations & Analytics

  • Own the tools and processes required to measure GTM experiments and growth initiatives
  • Maintain CRM hygiene, reporting, and dashboards that help the team understand performance and opportunities
  • Create visibility into experiment results, customer insights, and GTM learnings

What You Bring to the Table

  • 7–10+ years of growth marketing, GTM, product marketing, demand generation, or related experience within B2B SaaS or technology companies
  • Experience building GTM programs, growth motions, or new market initiatives from the ground up
  • Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous environments and create structure where processes do not yet exist
  • Strong experimentation mindset — comfortable developing hypotheses, testing assumptions, and making decisions based on imperfect data
  • Experience defining ICPs, segmentation strategies, positioning, and messaging
  • Strong understanding of customer acquisition strategies and what drives engagement in B2B markets
  • Comfortable partnering closely with Sales, Product Marketing, and Product teams
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to turn qualitative and quantitative insights into recommendations

Nice to have

  • Experience working on growth teams or product-led growth (PLG) initiatives
  • Experience building GTM strategies for emerging markets or new opportunities
  • Background in early-stage or high-growth technology companies
  • Familiarity with ABM strategies and account-level signal tracking
  • Experience spanning both growth marketing and product marketing disciplines

Why This Role

observations.title: Software Engineer II - Collaborative Web Platform

observations.description:
About Pantheon

Pantheon's WebOps Platform powers the open web, running more than 700,000 websites in the cloud for customers including Google, Princeton, Salesloft, and Doctors Without Borders. Every day, thousands of developers and marketers create, iterate, and scale WordPress and Drupal sites to reach billions of people globally. Pantheon's multi-tenant, container-based platform enables organizations to manage all of their websites from a single dashboard.

The Role

Pantheon is seeking a Staff Product Manager to lead how Pantheon delivers monetization and billing in the product, owning the infrastructure that turns pricing and packaging decisions into what customers actually experience — and using that ownership to move the metrics that matter with a high degree of independence. You'll build and run the billing, metering, and entitlement systems that make Pantheon's plans, tiers, and add-ons real, and use that platform to optimize what customers buy: driving upsell and expansion, and reducing downsell and churn.

You'll operate with minimal oversight, owning how Pantheon delivers and monetizes through the product — including how we enable partner and agency monetization — while partnering closely with Finance, RevOps, and Sales leadership on the underlying pricing and packaging decisions. You'll also mentor other PMs working on adjacent growth and monetization initiatives. The job is measured on outcomes: NRR, expansion, and reduced churn/downsell, and on the strength of the strategy and infrastructure you build to deliver them.

What You'll Do

  • Own net revenue retention (NRR) for the WebOps Platform: drive expansion and upsell, shape how packaging and tiers show up in-product, and reduce downsell and churn
  • Own and report on the metrics that matter: NRR, expansion revenue, and partner-sourced revenue, in partnership with Finance and Analytics
  • Partner cross-functionally on pricing and packaging strategy across self-serve, sales-assisted, and enterprise motions, bringing data and trade-off analysis to those decisions
  • Own the roadmap for Pantheon's billing and metering platform (subscription billing, invoicing, usage-based pricing, entitlements) as the infrastructure that makes those pricing and packaging decisions real
  • Keep billing, CRM, and quote-to-cash systems (Salesforce, HubSpot, and our billing platform) aligned so partner and customer pricing changes flow through cleanly to quotes, invoices, and revenue reporting
  • Reduce revenue leakage through payment, dunning, and collections improvements
  • Own how Pantheon enables partner and agency monetization by building the billing, discounting, and revenue-share mechanics that make it profitable for agencies to partner with us, in partnership with the Partner team, Sales, and Finance on the underlying terms
  • Track competitive and market trends in SaaS pricing, packaging, and billing to spot new monetization opportunities for Pantheon
  • Mentor and unblock other PMs working on adjacent growth and monetization initiatives, and champion pricing and billing best practices across the Product org
  • Build visibility and trust for monetization and billing work across the organization — communicating strategy, outcomes, and trade-offs clearly enough that leaders across Product, Finance, and Go-to-Market can act on them

What You Bring to the Table

Experience

  • 8+ years of Product Management experience, with deep expertise owning pricing, packaging, monetization, or billing at a B2B SaaS company, and a track record of driving strategic monetization initiatives with high independence
  • Experience designing partner, channel, or reseller pricing and incentive models — you know how to structure a deal that works for both sides
  • Direct experience owning or working closely with subscription billing platforms (e.g., Zuora, Chargebee, Stripe Billing, or similar)
  • Familiarity with usage-based pricing and metering/entitlement tools (e.g., Stigg, Metronome, Amberflo, or similar)
  • Working knowledge of CRM and quote-to-cash tooling (Salesforce, HubSpot) and how pricing changes flow through to sales and marketing systems
  • Demonstrated ability to design and interpret pricing experiments, and to use data (SQL, Amplitude, Looker, or similar) to inform monetization decisions
  • Proven ability to move revenue outcomes: NRR, expansion, and reduced churn/downsell
  • Skilled at leading cross-functional alignment across Engineering, Finance, RevOps, and Sales on monetization strategy, and comfortable operating with minimal direction
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills; resourceful, self-motivated, and detail-oriented

Bonus Points For

  • Experience monetizing a partner, agency, or channel ecosystem specifically
  • Background partnering directly with Finance/Revenue Accounting on billing system migrations or ERP integrations
  • Experience with WebOps, hosting, or the WordPress/Drupal ecosystem

What We Offer

  • Paid Time Off (PTO), Paid Sick Leave (PSL), and 11 Paid Company Holidays
